column4: 今天下雨，我的衣服都湿了。
column5: It rained today, and my clothes are all wet.
column6: 湿 means wet or damp: 湿衣服 (wet clothes), 湿了 (has got wet), 湿的 (wet). The opposite is 干.

column3: to break up; to be heartbroken
column5: He has gone through a break-up, and he is in a very bad mood.
column6: 失恋 is to lose a love, when a relationship ends and you are sad: 失恋了 (to be heartbroken). It is a verb-object word, so no object follows it.

column5: He had insomnia last night.
column6: 失眠 is to be unable to sleep, or insomnia: 失眠了 (had a sleepless night), 经常失眠 (to often have trouble sleeping).

column5: He is a famous poet.
column6: 诗人 is a poet: 一位诗人, 有名的诗人 (a famous poet). 诗 is a poem.

column4: 他在比赛中出现了两个失误。
column5: He made two mistakes in the match.
column6: 失误 is a mistake or slip in an action, often in sport or work: 出现失误 (to make an error), 一个失误 (a mistake). 错误 is a wrong answer or idea.

column5: He lost his job last year.
column6: 失业 is to lose one's job: 失业了 (lost a job), 失业的人 (unemployed people). It is a verb-object word.

column4: 从中国到美国有很大的时差。
column5: There is a big time difference between China and the USA.
column6: 时差 is the time difference between two places: 有时差 (to have jet lag), 时差很大 (a big time difference), 时差问题 (a jet lag problem).

column5: He often calls me.
column6: 时常 means often, and is a written word: 时常来 (to come often), 时常想起 (to often think of). 常常 is the everyday word.

column5: This is a new era.
column6: 时代 is an era or period in history: 新时代 (a new era), 那个时代 (that era), 时代不同了 (the times have changed). 年代 is a decade.

column5: When learning Chinese you need more practice.
column6: 实践 is to practise something in real life: 多实践 (to practise more), 实践经验 (practical experience), 社会实践 (practice in society).

column5: This is the most important moment.
column6: 时刻 is a moment: 重要时刻 (an important moment), 快乐的时刻 (a happy moment). As an adverb it means "at every moment": 时刻准备着 (always ready).

column5: This team has great strength.
column6: 实力 is real strength or ability: 有实力 (to have real ability), 实力强 (strong), 比赛实力 (competitive strength).

column4: 这是他一生中最难的时期。
column5: This is the hardest period of his life.
column6: 时期 is a period of time with its own character: 特殊时期 (a special period), 学生时期 (school days), 困难时期 (a hard time).

column5: The school has carried out a new method.
column6: 实施 is to carry out a plan or rule: 实施计划 (to carry out a plan), 开始实施 (to start being carried out). 实行 is to practise a system; 实现 is to make a goal come true.

column5: This stone is very heavy.
column6: 石头 is a stone or rock: 一块石头 (a stone), 大石头 (a big rock).

column5: He is doing an internship at a company.
column6: 实习 is to practise a job as a student: 去实习 (to go for an internship), 实习生 (an intern), 实习期 (an internship period).

column5: His dream has finally come true.
column6: 实现 is to make something real, or to come true: 实现梦想 (to realise a dream), 实现目标 (to achieve a goal).

column3: to carry out; to put into practice
column4: 这个城市实行新的办法。
column5: This city is putting a new method into practice.
column6: 实行 is to carry out a way of doing things in real life: 实行新办法 (to put a new method into practice), 已经实行 (already in force).

column4: 他们在做一个有意思的实验。
column5: They are doing an interesting experiment.
column6: 实验 is an experiment or to experiment: 做实验 (to do an experiment), 实验室 (a laboratory), 实验结果 (the result of an experiment).

column4: 同学们在实验室里做实验。
column5: The students are doing an experiment in the laboratory.
column6: 实验室 is a laboratory: 在实验室 (in the lab), 学校的实验室 (the school lab).

column5: This thing is very practical.
column6: 实用 means practical and useful in real life: 实用的东西 (a practical thing), 很实用 (very practical). 有用 is "useful".

column5: This kind of fruit can be eaten.
column6: 食用 means to eat, or edible, in formal writing: 可以食用 (can be eaten), 不能食用 (not for eating).

column5: Heavy rain makes the road hard to walk on.
column6: 使得 means "to make, to cause" and is followed by a result: 使得大家很高兴 (to make everyone happy). It is formal; 让 is the everyday word.

column3: all along; from start to finish
column5: He did not give up from start to finish.
column6: 始终 means "all along, from the beginning to the end": 始终没有 (never at any time), 始终相信 (to believe all along).

column5: He likes this way of life.
column6: 式 at the end of a word means a style, type or way: 方式 (way), 形式 (form).

column4: 适当运动对身体有好处。
column5: Suitable exercise is good for the body.
column6: 适当 means suitable or proper: 适当的时间 (a suitable time), 适当休息 (to take a proper rest).

column4: 他高兴得像个孩子似的。
column5: He is so happy that he is like a child.
column6: 似的 comes at the end and means "as if, like": 像……似的 (as if). It is often used with 像.

column5: An accident happened on the road.
column6: 事故 is an accident, usually with damage or injury: 发生事故 (an accident happens), 交通事故 (a traffic accident).

column4: 这个事件很快就过去了。
column5: This incident soon passed.
column6: 事件 is an event or incident, usually important or unusual: 重要事件 (an important event), 历史事件 (a historical event).

column5: The teacher is handing out the exam papers.
column6: 试卷 is an exam paper: 发试卷 (to hand out papers), 一张试卷 (an exam paper), 做试卷 (to do an exam paper).

column4: 这个城市的市民都很友好。
column5: The citizens of this city are all very friendly.
column6: 市民 are the people living in a city: 城市的市民 (the city's residents), 一位市民 (a resident).

column5: This is a fact.
column6: 事实 is a fact, what really happens: 事实上 (in fact), 不是事实 (not true), 说明事实 (to state the facts).

column5: Everyone regards him as a friend.
column6: 视为 means "to regard as", in writing: 视为朋友 (to regard as a friend), 把……视为 (to treat … as). It is formal.

column4: 孩子对新事物很有兴趣。
column5: Children are very interested in new things.
column6: 事物 means things and affairs in general, even abstract ones: 新事物 (new things), 各种事物 (all kinds of things). 东西 is a thing you can touch.

column5: Please tell me beforehand.
column6: 事先 means "in advance, beforehand": 事先准备 (to prepare in advance), 事先告诉 (to tell beforehand). 先 is "first".

column4: 他们在试验一种新方法。
column5: They are trying out a new method.
column6: 试验 is to test something new: 试验新方法 (to try a new method), 一次试验 (one trial). 实验 is a science experiment; 试验 is to test.

column5: His career is very successful.
column6: 事业 is a career or cause that a person works for: 事业成功 (a successful career), 重视事业 (to value one's career). 事业 is bigger than a 工作 (job).

column4: 这个手机可以试用三天。
column5: This phone can be tried out for three days.
column6: 试用 is to try something for a short time before buying or deciding: 试用期 (a trial period), 免费试用 (a free trial).

column4: 这个办法对每个人都适用。
column5: This method suits everyone.
column6: 适用 means suitable for use: 适用于 (applicable to), 不适用 (not suitable), 适用于孩子 (suits children).

column4: 这次旅行，我收获了很多。
column5: I gained a lot from this trip.
column6: 收获 is a harvest, or what you gain: 收获很大 (to gain a lot), 秋天收获 (to harvest in autumn).

column5: He likes collecting old photos.
column6: 收集 is to collect things over time: 收集信息 (to gather information), 收集照片 (to collect photos).

column5: Welcome to watch today's programme.
column6: 收看 is to watch TV or an online programme, as a formal word: 收看节目 (to watch a programme), 欢迎收看 (welcome to watch).

column5: The dog is guarding the house at the door.
column6: 守 is to guard (守门), to keep a promise (守约) and to stay on duty: 守着 (to be keeping watch), 守住 (to hold on to).

column5: This is the first time he has come to China.
column6: 首次 means "the first time", in writing: 首次见面 (to meet for the first time), 首次出国 (to go abroad for the first time). 第一次 is the everyday phrase.

column5: This kind of method is not good.
column6: 手段 is a means of getting something done, sometimes with a bad feeling: 不好的手段 (a bad method), 用各种手段 (to use all kinds of means). 办法 is a neutral way.

column5: This cup is handmade.
column6: 手工 is handwork, made by hand: 手工做 (made by hand), 手工课 (a handicraft class), 手工的 (handmade).

column5: He will have an operation tomorrow.
column6: 手术 is a medical operation: 做手术 (to have an operation), 手术成功 (a successful operation).

column5: It has got cold, so I need to wear gloves.
column6: 手套 are gloves: 一双手套 (a pair of gloves), 戴手套 (to wear gloves).

column5: Going through the formalities requires an ID card.
column6: 手续 are the official steps for getting something done: 办手续 (to go through the formalities), 手续简单 (simple procedures).

column5: His fingers are very long.
column6: 手指 is a finger: 一个手指 (a finger), 十个手指 (ten fingers).

column4: 这个杯子的售价是三十元。
column5: The selling price of this cup is thirty yuan.
column6: 售价 is the price at which something is sold: 售价高 (a high price), 原来的售价 (the original price). 价格 is the general word for "price".

column5: Eating more vegetables is good for the body.
column6: 蔬菜 are vegetables: 新鲜蔬菜 (fresh vegetables), 吃蔬菜 (to eat vegetables). 青菜 is leafy greens.

column5: He practises calligraphy every day.
column6: 书法 is calligraphy, the art of writing characters: 练习书法 (to practise calligraphy), 书法比赛 (a calligraphy competition).

column5: Dad is reading in the study.
column6: 书房 is a study at home: 在书房 (in the study), 一间书房 (a study).

column5: There are many books on the bookshelf.
column6: 书架 is a bookshelf: 一个书架, 书架上 (on the shelf).

column5: Please enter your name.
column6: 输入 is to put information into a computer or phone: 输入密码 (to enter a password), 输入汉字 (to type characters).

column5: This room is very comfortable.
column6: 舒适 means comfortable and pleasant: 舒适的房间 (a comfortable room), 舒适的生活 (a comfortable life). 舒服 is the everyday word, and also describes how you feel.

column5: He is very skilled at using a computer.
column6: 熟练 means skilled through practice: 熟练地说 (to speak fluently), 熟练使用 (to use skilfully), 技术熟练 (skilled technique).

column4: 我在路上遇到了一个熟人。
column5: I met an acquaintance on the road.
column6: 熟人 is someone you know: 遇到熟人 (to meet someone you know), 不是熟人 (not an acquaintance). 陌生人 is a stranger.

column5: This mouse is very easy to use.
column6: 鼠标 is a computer mouse: 一个鼠标, 用鼠标 (to use a mouse), 点鼠标 (to click the mouse).

column5: This book belongs to me.
column6: 属于 is to belong to: 属于我 (belongs to me), 不属于 (does not belong to).

column5: He gave her a bunch of flowers.
column6: 束 is a measure word for things tied in a bunch: 一束花 (a bunch of flowers), 一束光 (a beam of light).

column5: This data is very important.
column6: 数据 is data: 数据很多 (a lot of data), 看数据 (to look at the data).

column5: There are many trees on the mountain.
column6: 树木 means trees in general: 保护树木 (to protect trees), 树木很多 (many trees). 树 is one tree.

column3: to fall; to drop and break
column5: The child fell and cried.
column6: 摔 is to fall down, or to throw down and break: 摔了 (fell), 摔坏 (to break by dropping).

column5: Both sides agree to this method.
column6: 双方 means "both sides": 双方同意 (both sides agree), 比赛双方 (the two teams).

column5: Fruit has a lot of water in it.
column6: 水分 is the water in something: 水分多 (juicy), 补充水分 (to replenish water).

column5: He paid a lot of tax this year.
column6: 税 is tax: 交税 (to pay tax), 收税 (to collect tax).

column5: Sleep is very important for the body.
column6: 睡眠 is sleep, seen as a health matter: 睡眠不好 (poor sleep), 睡眠时间 (sleep time).

column5: Everything is going smoothly today.
column6: 顺 means "smooth" (很顺), "along" (顺着路走, to walk along the road) and "in passing" (顺便).

column5: Perhaps he has already gone home.
column6: 说不定 means "maybe, it could be": 说不定会下雨 (it may rain). It shows you are not sure. 也许 is similar.

column5: I want to persuade him to stay.
column6: 说服 is to persuade by giving reasons: 说服他 (to persuade him), 被说服 (to be convinced). 劝 is gentle advice; 说服 changes someone's mind.

column4: 他在认真地思考这个问题。
column5: He is thinking seriously about this question.
column6: 思考 is to think carefully: 认真思考 (to think seriously), 思考问题 (to think about a problem). 想 is the everyday word.

column5: This is my private phone.
column6: 私人 means private or personal: 私人电话 (a private phone), 私人时间 (private time), 私人问题 (a personal question).

column5: Her thinking is very quick.
column6: 思维 is thinking as a mental process: 思维方式 (way of thinking), 思维很快 (quick thinking).

column4: 这本书里的思想很有意思。
column5: The ideas in this book are very interesting.
column6: 思想 is thought or ideas: 新思想 (new ideas), 思想很新 (very new ideas). 想法 is "an idea" in daily speech; 思想 is bigger, like a system of ideas.
